# Menina

> Self-hosted application platform: point container images at it, it runs them on
> k3s and routes public hostnames (HTTP + raw TCP/UDP) through its own proxy.

Menina is one Go binary with distinct modes. Desired state is human-editable YAML
(`/etc/menina`); operational state is SQLite (`/var/lib/menina`). `menina serve`
is the control plane (single SQLite writer, config watcher, registry listener,
reconciler); `menina proxy` serves traffic. Deploys happen by pushing images to
the bundled registry.

## Install and provision

```bash
curl -fsSL https://menina.moureau.dev/install.sh | sudo sh   # installs binary + systemd units (does not provision)
sudo menina setup            # write config.yml (interactive; --non-interactive for defaults)
sudo menina deploy           # provision k3s, registry, control plane, proxy (idempotent)
```

Root is needed for `install`, `setup`, `deploy`, `upgrade`, and
`backup --with-volumes/--with-images`. Day-to-day commands run as any user in
the `menina` group. Interactive menus/prompts need a TTY; automation must use
flags (see "Automation: SSH and CI").

## Concepts

- **Project** — a unit of config (`projects/<name>/`). Has a namespace (default
  `menina-apps`).
- **Environment** — a deployment target (`production`, `staging`, ...). Each env
  gets its own namespace `<project-ns>-<env>` unless overridden. Holds per-app
  overrides and exposure.
- **App** — a container image + workload (service or worker) + scaling/storage.
- **Registry** — bundled Zot at `registry.<domain>`; pushing an image triggers
  an automatic deploy of matching apps. There is **one shared push/pull
  credential** (k3s pulls with the same username/password).

## Config layout

```text
/etc/menina/
  config.yml
  projects/<project>/
    project.yml                 # name, namespace, description
    apps/<app>.yml              # shared app definition
    environments/<env>.yml      # environment definition (optional)
    environments/<env>/<app>.yml  # per-app override (one file per app)
/var/lib/menina/                # menina.db, certs/, releases/, backups/
```

## App definition (`apps/<app>.yml`)

```yaml
name: api
source: { repo: github.com/acme/api }                    # owning repo; blank/omitted = locally owned
image: { repository: registry.example.com/my-app/api }   # repository is immutable (per app)
workload: { type: service, port: 8080 }                  # type: service|worker; command/args optional
resources: { cpu: 250m, memory: 256Mi }                  # requests == limits
replicas: 1                                              # or {min: 2, max: 10, targetCPU: 70} -> HPA
storage: { enabled: true, size: 1Gi, mountPath: /data }  # PVC <app>-data
health: { readiness: /healthz }                          # HTTP probes
env: { RUST_LOG: info }
secrets: { DATABASE_URL: "file:/etc/menina/secrets/db" } # env var -> secret ref (never plaintext)
```

`menina app create` defaults `image.repository` to the bundled registry as
`registry.<domain>/<project>/<app>`; `--repository` overrides it.

## Environment (`environments/<env>.yml` + `environments/<env>/<app>.yml`)

Only config here opts a host in (exposure is environment-level). An environment
may be declared by a definition file (`<env>.yml`) and/or a directory of
per-app override files (`<env>/<app>.yml`, one app per file); directory
overrides win over an inline `apps:` map. Splitting per app lets several repos
contribute to one environment without writing the same file. `image.repository`
cannot be overridden; other fields merge (override wins).

```yaml
name: production
apps:
  api:
    enabled: true
    image: { tag: production }        # default tag = environment name (defaults.imageTagStrategy)
    replicas: { min: 2, max: 10 }
    exposure:
      enabled: true
      hosts: [api.example.com]
      pathPrefix: /
      headers: { X-Frame-Options: DENY }
      compression: false
      h2c: false                      # cleartext HTTP/2 to the backend (gRPC)
      maxBodyBytes: 0
      timeouts: { read: 30s, write: 60s, idle: 120s }
      ports: { tcp: [25565], udp: [19132] }   # raw L4 ports (bypass proxy)
```

An app is only reachable when its env override sets `enabled: true` **and**
`exposure.hosts` (or `exposure.ports`); then run `menina app deploy <app>
--project <p> --environment <env>`.

## Common tasks

```bash
# Create a project (+ environments), then an app, then make it public
menina create my-app --yes --environments production,staging   # or bare `menina` menu
menina app create api --project my-app --port 8080 --yes       # repository defaults to the registry
# edit my-app/environments/production.yml: api.enabled=true, api.exposure.hosts=[api.example.com]
menina app deploy api --project my-app --environment production --yes

# Get everything CI needs (registry host + push username/password)
menina registry credential --json          # {"domain","username","password"}

# Push an image -> auto-deploys matching enabled apps
HOST=registry.<domain>
USER=$(menina registry credential --username)
menina registry credential --password | docker login "$HOST" -u "$USER" --password-stdin
docker build -t "$HOST/my-app/api:production" .
docker push  "$HOST/my-app/api:production"
```

## CLI

```bash
# projects / envs / apps
menina create                                # guided: prompts name, environments
menina create my-project --yes --environments development,staging,production
menina project create <name> --environments a,b  |  menina project list
menina environment create <env> --project <p>    |  menina environment list --project <p>
menina app create api --project <p> --repository <repo> --port 8080 --yes
menina app list --project <p>
menina app edit api --project <p>            # $EDITOR

# deploy / operate
menina app deploy api --project <p> --environment <env> --yes   # waits for rollout
menina app logs api --project <p> --environment <env> --follow
menina app rollback api --project <p> --environment <env> [--digest sha256:...]
menina app scale api --project <p> --min 2 --max 10              # baseline (all envs)
menina app scale api --project <p> -e production --replicas 4    # one environment
menina app delete api --project <p>            # soft: stop + keep config; --hard removes+prunes
menina app restore api --project <p>

# secrets (values read from stdin, never printed)
printf '%s' "$DATABASE_URL" | menina secret set DATABASE_URL --project <p> --environment <env>
menina secret list --project <p> --environment <env>      # names only
menina secret remove DATABASE_URL --project <p> --environment <env> --yes

# observe / infra
menina status [--json]               # includes the registry host
menina routes [--json]               # HTTP routes + L4 TCP/UDP exposures
menina doctor                        # config, k8s, registry, routes, TLS checks
menina registry status
menina registry credential [--username | --password | --regenerate]
menina notify list | menina notify test [--project <p>]
menina backup [--out f.tgz --with-secrets --with-volumes --with-images --consistent --passphrase]
menina restore <f.tgz> --force [--with-volumes --with-images]
menina upgrade [--check]
```

Most list/status commands accept `--json` for machine-readable output.
`menina registry credential --username`/`--password` print just that field;
`--regenerate` rotates the shared credential (and re-applies it to Zot and k3s);
`--new-username`/`--new-password` set explicit values when regenerating.

## Automation: SSH and CI

**SSH / remote VPS.** Menina runs on the host; drive it over SSH. Interactive
flows need a real TTY (`ssh -t`); a command without `-t` gets no TTY and falls
back to flags/help, so scripts must pass flags. Use `--json` instead of parsing
tables, and `sudo` for root-only commands.

```bash
ssh host sudo menina deploy                  # root-only, non-interactive
ssh host menina status --json                # machine-readable; includes "registry"
ssh -t host menina                           # interactive menu (needs a TTY)
```

**CI (build & push only).** CI needs no Menina binary, no `/etc/menina`, no root
and no TTY — just the registry host plus the username/password. Discover them
once on the host and store them as CI secrets:

```bash
menina registry credential --json   # {"domain":"registry.<domain>","username":"...","password":"..."}
```

Then the job is plain Docker:

```bash
echo "$REGISTRY_PASSWORD" | docker login "$REGISTRY_HOST" -u "$REGISTRY_USER" --password-stdin
docker build -t "$REGISTRY_HOST/$PROJECT/$APP:$TAG" .
docker push  "$REGISTRY_HOST/$PROJECT/$APP:$TAG"     # triggers a deploy of matching apps
```

For the push to deploy, the app's `image.repository` must equal
`$REGISTRY_HOST/$PROJECT/$APP` and `image.tag` must equal `$TAG` (tag defaults to
the environment name). If the registry serves **HTTP** (`tls.mode: none`), the
CI Docker daemon must list `$REGISTRY_HOST` in `insecure-registries`.

## Interactive (TTY only)

Bare `menina` opens a full-screen menu (Setup / Deploy / apps / status / ...).
`menina app` / `project` / `environment` open project → app → action menus
(`Deploy · Scale · Edit · Logs · Rollback · Delete · Back`); selectors include
`Exit`. Arrow keys move **one row at a time**, `/` filters, `Enter` selects,
`Shift+Tab`/`Esc` goes **back** (menus step up; inline flows like "new app name"
return to their list), and **`Ctrl+C` must be pressed twice** to quit. Once the
platform is ready the one-time Setup/Deploy entries are hidden unless
`--show-all` is passed. Non-TTY/pipes and `--yes` use flags only.

## Deploy pipeline

1. `docker push registry.<domain>/<project>/<app>:<tag>`.
2. Zot emits an event; `menina serve` matches enabled apps by repository + tag.
3. The tag is resolved to an immutable **digest**; the Deployment is updated to
   `repo@sha256:...` (rollback restores a recorded digest).
4. `menina deploy` reconciles k3s/Zot/services; a periodic reconciler applies
   desired state and prunes removed workloads (PVCs and history are retained).

## Scaling

- Baseline `replicas` in the app file; per-environment override in the env file.
- `{min,max,targetCPU}` ⇒ a `HorizontalPodAutoscaler`; a fixed count removes any
  stale HPA. `menina app scale` writes baseline or `-e <env>` override;
  `--reset` removes the override.

## TLS and networking

- `tls.terminate: true` + `tls.mode: acme` ⇒ Menina issues a **per-hostname**
  Let's Encrypt cert automatically for every routed host and **auto-renews**
  (`httpRedirect: false` serves `:80` and `:443` with no forced redirect/HSTS).
- `tls.mode: none` ⇒ HTTP only (e.g. behind a proxy). Pushing to an HTTP registry
  requires `insecure-registries` on the client.
- Wildcards are **not** supported (ACME is HTTP-01/TLS-ALPN-01, not DNS-01).
- Cloudflare: orange cloud + **Flexible** if the origin is HTTP-only; or run
  origin ACME and use **Full (strict)**. Keep `registry.<domain>` **DNS-only
  (grey)** so pushes aren't capped by the CF proxy (100 MB / ~100 s).

## L4 (non-HTTP) exposure

`exposure.ports` binds raw ports on the node via `hostPort` (bypassing the proxy)
— for game servers, TURN/STUN, etc. Accepts a number, list, or `{tcp, udp}`.
Ports 80/443 are reserved; duplicate host ports are rejected. `menina deploy`
opens them with `ufw` when active. Keep L4 apps at 1 replica (hostPort is
per-pod). gRPC works over the HTTP proxy via `exposure.h2c: true`.

## Backup and migration

`menina backup` → portable `tar.gz` (DB + `config.yml` + `projects/`; opt-in
`--with-secrets` [encryptable via `--passphrase`], `--with-volumes`,
`--with-images`; `--consistent` quiesces writers). `menina restore <f.tgz>
--force` applies it (stop the writer first: `systemctl stop menina-serve`).

## Not supported (today)

No HTTP/3/QUIC, no ACME wildcards, no built-in auth/rate-limiting/WAF, no
multi-node k3s or HA control plane (SQLite is a single writer; `local-path`
volumes are node-local), no canary/blue-green strategies, no cron/one-off jobs,
and no per-user registry credentials (one shared push/pull credential).
